raw_response:
I would keep my land in the usual Quzhou grain rotation: `winter wheat -> summer maize`. In Quzhou County, that is still the most reliable way for me to use the whole year, and the local work on wheat-maize production shows this system fits the area well. I am 60, so I would not chase a complicated cash crop this year. I would choose the familiar crops I can manage with machinery, stable buyers, and steady output. I would use an improved wheat variety and a hybrid maize variety, keep fertilizer moderate instead of pushing too hard on nitrogen, return straw, irrigate only at the key stages, and spray only when disease or insects are likely to cost yield. For tillage, I would use rotary tillage before wheat and no-tillage direct seeding for summer maize after wheat harvest, because that saves labor and fits the local double-cropping rhythm. I am basing this on the Quzhou wheat-maize system and local Hebei guidance on fertilization and water-saving management: https://www.agri.cn/zx/xxlb/hb/202410/t20241011_8677909.htm , https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/2/25/art_46232_1012984.html , https://www.moa.gov.cn/gk/nszd_1/2023/202309/t20230928_6437567.htm , https://www.zynylm.com/zhibao/2019/0222/3071.html
